Pulled from the Consent  discussion.
Calendar for Further Discussion
  Rotation to Mayor Pro Tern — The  City Council has followed a formal
  procedure for the  rotation of the office of Mayor Pro Tern since 1993 and
  reaffirm that policy annually. According to Resolution No. 16- 19, the current
  established rotation policy, the office of Mayor Pro Tern rotates to Council
  Member Robin Carder for a one- year term or until the second  Council
  meeting in March 2020.

  Council Member Carder recommended that Council Member Rosales be
  appointed Mayor Pro Tern since he will be retiring from the Council and this will
  be his last year. She stated this would be a way to honor him and make his last
  year memorable and she will be placed next on the rotation list for Mayor Pro
  Tern.

  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Kendrick, and carried by a vote of 4- 0,
  Davis absent) to appoint Charlie Rosales as Mayor Pro Tern for a one- year
  term, or until the second Council meeting in March 2020 and that Council
  Member Carder will be placed next on the rotation list for Mayor Pro Tern.

Tract  Map  No.  53984;  Tract  Map No.  53984: Puddingstone Hill Bond  Reduction - The
Puddingstone Hill Bond  developer  of  Puddingstone Hill ( Tract Map No. 53984), a 15 Lot single family
Reduction  subdivision at the terminus of De Anza Heights Road ( Private Street) has
  requested a second reduction of their performance  sureties for work
  completed to date. Staff has inspected the required public/ private
  improvements constructed to date and it is in conformance with the approved
  plans.

  Staff recommended that the City Council authorize the reduction of the
  performance sureties requirements for Tract Map No. 53984 to
  approximately 24 percent of their value. Approved as recommended by

Parcel Map No. 76069,  parcel Map No. 76069. ( La Verne Landing. LLC) - Approval of Subdivision
La Verne Landing, LLC)  Agreement-  On February 19, 2019, the City Council approved Final Parcel
  Map No. 76069 ( Case 57- 17 TPM) to consolidate eight parcels into a single
  parcel to allow for an apartment building to be built over the proposed site by
  WF Construction. The Subdivision Agreement had not been submitted in time
  by the Developer to be included in City Council packet.

  Staff recommended that the City Council authorize the Assistant City
  Clerk and the Mayor to execute the Subdivision Agreement for Final Parcel
  Map No. 76069, La Verne Landing, LLC( WF Construction).  Approved as

  recommended by staff.

Ambulance Replacement  Ambulance Replacement- The Fire Department and Fleet Division are
  recommending the replacement of the City' s 2009 Ambulance from allocated
  public safety equipment funds. Authorization is requested to replace the
  ambulance prior to the start of the 2019/ 20 fiscal year due to ongoing
  operational needs.

  Staff recommended that the Council approve and appropriate total replacement
  costs of$ 238,600; authorizing the City Manager to execute a purchase order
  and agreement with  Braun Northwest in the amount of$ 215, 977 for the
  purchase of a Type I Ambulance, which is a piggyback on a competitively
  awarded contract by the City of El Segundo; and Transfer the needed funding
  of$ 125, 000 and $ 113, 600 from funds 405 and 250 respectively. Approved as

  recommended by staff.

Housing Element Annual  housing Element Annual Progress Reports - 2013 to 2016 and 2018 - The
Progress Reports - 2013 to  City is required to prepare an Annual Progress Report on the status and
2016 and 2018  progress in implementing its Housing Element. This Report is required to be
  presented to the City Council prior to submitting the report to the State. A
  review of the file found that previous years reports were not filed, so in order
  to be fully compliant, staff has prepared the reports for 2013 to 2016 and 2018.

  Staff recommended that the City Council authorized the Community
  Development  Department staff to submit Annual Progress Reports for 2013 to
  2016 and 2018. Approved as recommended by staff.

Resolution No. 19- 09,  Resolution No. 19- 09 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
Authorizing a Project List as  CITY OF LA VERNE, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF
Required by Senate Bill 1: The  CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING A PROJECT LIST AS REQUIRED BY
Road Repair and Accountability  SENATE BILL 1:  THE ROAD REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT - In
Act  April 2017 Governor Brown signed into law Senate Bill 1 ( SB1),  also referred

  to as the Road Repair and Accountability Act ( RRAA) of 2017.  SB1 provides
  for increased gas taxes and registration fees, which are to be deposited into
  the State' s Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation Account ( RMRA).  RMRA
  funds are apportioned to local agencies each year for basic road
  maintenance, rehabilitation, and other safety projects. SB1 also requires
  each eligible agency to submit a project list to California Transportation
  Commission ( CTC) in order to receive these funds. La Verne' s allocation for
  fiscal year 2019/ 20 is estimated at$ 550, 507.

  Staff recommended City Council approval of Resolution No. 19- 09,
  approving the proposed SB1 project list for fiscal year 2019/ 20. Approved as
  recommended  by staff.
 City Council Minutes, Monday, March 18, 2019, Page 4

  La Verne and the County of Los Angeles will expire on June 30, 2019. The
  approval of this agreement will extend services for a period of five years,
  commencing July 1, 2019, through June 30, 2024 thereby allowing the City to
  contract with the County for various services.

  Staff recommended that the Council adopt Resolution No. 19- 10,

  of La Verne and the County of Los Angeles. Approved as recommended by

Resolution No. 19- 11,  Resolution No. 19- 11 -  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF

Southern California Velo, Inc.  CALIFORNIA, AUTHORZING THE  EXECUTION OF AN AGREEMENT
for the 2019 San Dimas Stage  WITH SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA VELO, INC FOR THE 2019 SAN DIMAS
Race  STAGE RACE - The Southern California VELO Cycling Club has submitted
  a request to use Puddingstone Drive for the purpose of a cycling race on
  Saturday, March 30, 2019. The request specifically involves the closure of
  the west and eastbound lanes of Puddingstone Drive from Wheeler
  Avenue to Fairplex Drive between the hours of 7: 30 a. m. and 6: 00 p. m. The
  race is expected to draw up to 1, 000 participants. Recent policy has been to
  prepare individualized agreements for such large events. Staff has therefore
  developed a standard agreement outlining the traffic control plan
  requirements,  locations, schedule,  estimated fees, applicant' s
  responsibilities, and insurance and indemnification requirements.

  Staff recommended that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19- 11,
  authorizing the City Manager to execute the Agreement with Southern
  California VELO Cycling Club permitting the Cycling race on specified
  streets.

Community Development Block  City Manager Russi reported on the Community Development Block Grant
  45tn

Grant Program for 2019- 2020  Program for 2019- 20.  He stated that is the
  funding year for the
  Community Development Block Grant Program. According to the Los
  Angeles County CDBG Bulletin, the City of La Verne will be allocated
  approximately $ 145, 000 in Community Development Block Grant( CDBG)
  funds. One application for a public service program has been received for
  consideration and an application from the Public Works Department for
  sidewalk repairs. Staff is continuing to work with the Community
  Development Commission to allocate the remaining portion of the grant to
  benefit the City of La Verne. He stated the Community Development
  Department is expecting to start a neighborhood revitalization program in the
  new fiscal year. Staff will bring a new program to Council in the near future for
  their approval.

  Council Member Carder spoke about the Senior Lunch Program and asked
  Recreation Coordinator Duran to elaborate on the program.

  Yvonne Duran reported on the Senior Lunch Program explaining the cost was
  1, lunch is served Monday through Fridays, and seniors must call to make a
  reservation.

  Mayor Kendrick opened the public hearing and called for public comment on
  this matter.

  There was none.

  Mayor Kendrick spoke about the new neighborhood revitalization program that
  will be started in the new fiscal year and that the program will allow the City to
  help people in the community that need help.

  Council Cember Hepburn also agreed that the new neighborhood revitalization
  program would help some residents fix their homes. He stated he was excited
  about this new program,

  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Hepburn, and carried by a vote of 4- 0,
  Davis absent) to approve the following allocation of the 2019- 2020
  Community Development Block Grant ( CDBG) funds of $ 145, 000 , as
  recommended by staff; as follows:

  Mid- Year Financial Report  Finance Manager Statham reported on the Mid- Year Financial Report-
  December 31. 2018  December 31, 2018. He stated that the Finance Division is providing a mid- year
  fiscal status report concerning the financial activities of the City for the period
  ending December 31, 2018. The report includes budget to actual comparisons
  for revenues and expenditures along with other financial information. Per his
  Staff report dated March 18, 2018, Finance Manager Statham reported on the
  Revenues by Source and Transfers, Property Tax Report, Sales Tax Revenue,
  Expenditures by Function and Budget Amendments. He stated that overall the
  City was online with the Budget. In addition, he reported the property values in
  La Verne are very good and it shows that people want to live in La Verne.

  Council Member Hepburn stated that he appreciates the Mid- Year Financial
  Report and that it shows what' s happening in the City and it really helps
  pinpoint where the City stands financially.

  Council Member Carder agreed with Council Member Hepburn and the Mid-
  Year Financial Report does have more detail. She stated she was pleased with
  the property values in La Verne. In addition, she stated that it was wonderful to
  have Gilead Sciences in the City and the City was very fortunate to have them.

  Mayor Pro Tern Rosales stated he too was happy about the property values in
  La Verne and that La Verne is a wonderful community.

  Mayor Kendrick stated that the City of La Verne has good housing stock and
  people want to live in La Verne. He stated he too appreciated the new Mid-
  Year Financial Report which contained lots of information and knowing that the
  City is doing what it is supposed to be doing.

  It was moved by Hepburn, seconded by Carder, and carried by a vote of 4- 0
  Davis absent) approve the budget amendments detailed in the included
  Budget Amendments listing to adjust revenues and expenditure
  appropriations for the fiscal year 2018/ 19 budget. The Council also received
  and filed the December 31, 2018 Mid- Year Financial Report.

6.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda. Mayor Kendrick called for
  public comment.

  Gary Hunter, Chelsea Drive, La Verne, stated he really appreciated the new
  LED streetlights and that it was good decision by the City.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, March 18, 2019, Page 7

7.  Council Comments and  Council Member Hepburn reported on the San Gabriel Valley Council of
  Meeting/ Conference Reports  Government meeting. He reported that funding for the City of La Verne' s Gold
  Line Transit Oriented Pedestrian Bridge has been approved.  The pedestrian
  bridge would span Arrow Highway and the adjacent parallel Metrolink railroad
  tracks. The bridge will connect La Verne' s Gold Line Station to the northern
  edge of the Fairplex property. In addition he reported that new legislation is
  being proposed to address the costs to local jurisdictions regarding the MS- 4
  Permit ( Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System) regulations and
  requirements.

  Mayor Pro Rosales thanked Council Member Hepburn for his report on the
  proposed legislation for MS- 4 Permit requirements and stated it is a very
  important matter that should be of concern to everyone because of the huge
  cost involved in implemting the new requirements. In addition, he thanked
  Council Member Carder for her work on the Gold Line Construction Committee
  and spoke of the many accolades he hears about her work on the committee.

  Council Member Carder reported on the Gold Line Construction meeting. She
  reported that currently the project is stagnate, but slowly moving, and to expect
  to see more activity in 2020. In addition, she reported on La Verne Little
  League Opening Day. She stated it was an amazing day and she thanked the
  Parks staff for the great job they do in maintaining the fields.

  Mayor Kendrick also thanked Council Member Hepburn for his report and
  efforts on the pedestrian bridge. He reported on Hillcrest Good Samaritan
  Dinner and La Verne Heights Elementary School tours of City Hall. He thanked
  Personnel Officer Ranells, Community Development Director Scherer and
  Planning Intern Lauren Augino for being tour guides.

8  Adjournment at 7 27 pm., in memory of Ed Forbes, former La Verne Resident and builder. " He left his mark in
  La Verne and will be missed" quoted by Council Member Rosales.
